data.one_liner: Build and bundle Rust code into a Dart/Flutter project via build hooks.
data.what_it_does: It automates compiling Rust libraries for all supported platforms and packages the binaries as assets that Dart can load. The only required input is the asset name; the rest is inferred from Cargo.toml and rust-toolchain.toml.
use_when: You need native performance or system libraries written in Rust.
You want reproducible builds across Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, and Linux.
You prefer a declarative build setup over manual Cargo commands.
avoid_when: You only target a single platform and prefer manual Cargo integration.
You need fine‑grained control over the Rust build process beyond what the hook offers.
strengths: Zero‑config Rust integration after initial Cargo setup.
Cross‑platform builds with a single command.
Automatic dependency discovery and rebuild triggers.
Supports both staticlib and cdylib targets.
weaknesses: Requires rustup and a Rust toolchain on the developer machine.
Limited to the platforms listed; adding new targets needs code changes.
data.setup_notes: Add rustup, create Cargo.toml and rust-toolchain.toml, run flutter pub add native_toolchain_rust hooks, then add a build.dart hook that calls RustBuilder.
